title: Days Until Warmer
statement:
`temps[i]` is the temperature on day `i`. For **each day**, find how many days you must wait until a **warmer** temperature arrives (strictly higher). If no later day is warmer, the answer for that day is `0`.

Return the list of waiting times, one number per day.

examples.explanation: Day 0 (73) waits 1 day for 74; day 2 (75) waits 4 days for 76; the last two days never see a warmer day.
Each day is followed by a warmer one, except the last.

hints.nudge: Days that are still waiting for a warmer day form a pattern: their temperatures never increase from first to last. Why?
hints.pattern: Monotonic stack of indices waiting for a warmer day.
hints.pseudocode:
stack = []  (indices of days still waiting)
for i, t in temps:
  while stack not empty and temps[top] < t: j = pop; result[j] = i - j
  push i
hints.walkthrough: Checking all later days for each day is O(n^2). Keep a stack of day indices that have not found a warmer day yet. Their temperatures are non-increasing from bottom to top (otherwise a warmer one would already have resolved the earlier ones). When day i arrives with temperature t, it resolves every waiting day colder than t: pop them and record i - index as their waiting time. Then push i. Each day is pushed and popped once, so O(n). Days left on the stack get 0.
